{{{hug}}}!!!

A-lines are flattering on everyone. I love them. If your legs are shorter, your skirt can be, too, though you also might want to go for something high-waisted and longer (like, knee-length) to make your legs look longer--pencil skirts often have high waists, and if they reach just below the knees they'll add length, too. But don't do below-the-knee if its waist hits you at or below your hips/wait, because that will make your legs look shorter. Pleats are also flattering on just about everyone--especially kick pleats--and are adorable, though I admit as I approach 46 I'm a leeetle unsure if I should still be wearing them. (I have two adorable kickpleat minis, but I kind of feel like I look like I'm trying to look too young if I wear them, you know?)

Leggings or tights in the same color as the skirt will also help make your legs look a little longer (and are helpful if you haven't shaved or aren't comfortable showing your legs yet). Or, if you want, you could go for an a-line or slim-fitting floor-length skirt, though you have to be careful with those because they can also make you look stumpy. It's worth trying one on and seeing if you like it. Just remember, if you're going for the maxiskirt, your top has to be minimal--no bulky sweaters or loose tops! You want a tank or slim-fit t-shirt, maybe with a snug cropped jacket or something at most. Otherwise you'll look like a big shapeless column. (Maxiskirts also are surprisingly warm and cozy in winter!)

Of course, the classic denim skirt also tends to look great on most people, and has the benefit of being casual enough that you don't feel dressed up wearing one. You can dress them up a little with heels or dress them way down with socks and tennis shoes. They work with any kind of top, too: big and bulky, slim and fitted, whatever. I treat mine just like jeans (although while my jeans are ALL black always, I have never owned a black denim skirt--those are always blue, in varying shades).

I am not a fan of a black casual skirt with bare legs, especially not with black shoes. I don't know why, it's just always bugged me. If I'm going to wear a black skirt I almost always have black tights underneath (unless it's a dressy outfit, in which case it doesn't bother me as much). My "bare legs" skirts are usually denim or different colors. The exception is if I'm wearing boots, in which case bare legs are fine (socks under the boots, of course, but they're not visible).
